links.outcome: Subspecialist preference and error rates for cardiologists with versus without AI assistance
links.effect: AMIE-assisted assessments preferred 46.7% vs 32.7% for cardiologists alone (P = 0.02); clinically significant errors 13.1% with AMIE vs 24.3% alone (P = 0.033).
links.quote: Subspecialists also quantified errors, extra and missing content, reasoning and potential bias.

links.outcome: Quality of triage, diagnosis, and management with versus without LLM assistance in randomized trial
links.effect: Subspecialists preferred AMIE-assisted assessments 46.7% vs 32.7% (P = 0.02); 20.6% tie; fewer errors and less missing content with AMIE.
links.quote: Overall, subspecialists preferred AMIE-assisted cardiology assessments 46.7% of the time, compared with 32.7% for cardiologists alone (P = 0.02), with 20.6% rated as a tie.

screen.reason: Randomized controlled trial evaluating clinician decision-making with vs without LLM assistance on retrospective complex cardiology cases.
